entries.content: I used to obsess over toggling permissions on and off, but honestly life got so much easier when I realized that granting access once basically signals to the app what you're comfortable with. My delivery apps, ride shares, weather apps—I gave them location when I first needed it, and keeping it on just means the experience stays smooth. Haven't had any issues in three years of doing this.

Mobile applications may collect location data for various purposes including service delivery, analytics, advertising, and feature personalization. The specific uses depend on the app's privacy policy and the permissions granted by the user.

Since you already granted location access for a legitimate security feature, the app is working as intended. Many users find that once they've established their permission preferences during initial setup or first use, maintaining those settings provides a consistent experience. The app uses this information to help protect your account, so the original permission continues to serve its purpose.

Transferred apps from old phone. Noticed permission prompts came up again during first use of each app. Realized these initial prompts are basically the app learning my preferences—once I tap Allow for something like location or camera, that's the app understanding what I need from it. Makes sense to just approve what I approved before since those were thoughtful decisions at the time.

Noticed my battery was draining faster than usual. Checked settings and found several apps were using location services in the background even when I wasn't actively using them. Changed a few to 'While Using' instead of 'Always' and saw improvement. Kind of annoying to go through each app though.
